scope: Independent complete read of the two Memory product files, their exact baseline diff, and the new 25-case test source. No Dart/Flutter execution, Android disk-failure experiment, or runtime acceptance.
findings: The original Android plugin returns Editor.commit() and getAll exposes native preferences memory. AOSP API35 changes mMap before the disk result. A successful reload alone is not a positive write acknowledgement.

The optional MemoryReadbackConfirmation interface is implemented by PreferencesMemoryStore. Its readRound/readStats remain read-only reload snapshots; positive confirmation is a separate same-value setString.

The controller validates an observed payload and checks the captured profile immediately before and after confirming it. open, initial-write recovery, uncertain subsequent reads, commit recovery and statistics adoption cannot substitute equality for a positive platform reply.

Negative or missing platform replies remain MemoryStorageUnconfirmed; false is distinguished as MemoryStorageRejected. Statistics confirmation failures propagate, while corrupt historical statistics remain untouched.

A failed action retains uncertainty. A bounded later positive same-value confirmation can adopt the same round and revision without a second flip, RNG draw or reward identity. No retry loop or key/schema/rule change was added.

The new test platform separates Dart's real cache, nativeMemory and durableDisk, models generation tracking and whole-file commits, and distinguishes a new Dart cache from a modeled native-process restart.

All 25 declared cases were read: raw snapshots after false/throw, initial creation, failed flip and subsequent uncertainty, new controller, modeled process restart, lost reply after commit, no-positive-reply failure, statistics, corruption, foreign owner, before/during-profile-loss guards, exact newer revision and three actual Memory-to-AppState/Wallet cases.

The three AppState integrations use actual Memory rules/controller/catalog, captured child lease and wallet repository. The final duplicate-wallet negative case explicitly requires Wallet737ba477; it must not be run against the unchanged 28462 Wallet and described as a Memory-only result.

The final integration avoids setting the same profile again after a failed wallet write, because any unrelated successful preference commit can legitimately flush the outstanding whole native preference file.
Existing 14-case durability test bytes remain exactly SHA7f81307b; no prior PASS result is transferred to the new 25 cases.

upstream_boundaries.same_value_commit: AOSP synchronous commit can retry an outstanding memory generation even when the value itself is unchanged. A positive reply is a platform acknowledgement, not a new independent physical-disk measurement.

limits: All new 25 test cases remain unexecuted in this review; actual combined CI is required.
The platform model is synthetic. It is not an Android fault-injection, fsync, power-loss or device restart experiment.
The existing owner queue serializes the current Dart runtime. This patch does not establish cross-engine compare-and-swap or arbitrary concurrent-writer correctness.
General Wallet.load/fallback behavior and cross-repository stale snapshots remain outside this narrow change.
